intervals.note: Earliest dated evidence for the collaboration's experiment (start of solar-neutrino measurement per the SAGE Collaboration's 2009 paper), not a formation date; the formation date is not sourced.
intervals.quote: The Russian-American experiment SAGE began to measure the solar neutrino capture rate with a target of gallium metal in December 1989.

leadership.locator: CERN Courier, "Baksan scales new neutrino heights" (19 May 2017), section on the gallium experiments
leadership.note: As of the May 2017 article; no start or end date is published. The article gives no formal title (such as spokesperson), so the role is 'other'.
leadership.quote: SAGE, which has been in operation since 1986 and is led by Vladimir Gavrin, is located 3.5 km from the tunnel entrance

leadership.note: Led the American side of the collaboration 'for many years'; no start or end date is published and no formal title is given, so the role is 'other'.
leadership.quote: We thank Thomas Bowles for leading the American side of the SAGE collaboration for many years

name: SAGE Collaboration
notes: No membership counts or dedicated official site were found in a source consulted (checked 2026-09-18). The author lists of the SAGE Collaboration's 2009 paper (arXiv:0901.2200) give the Institute for Nuclear Research of the Russian Academy of Sciences (Moscow), Los Alamos National Laboratory, the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the University of Washington, without claiming a full institution list.

summary.plain: The Russian-American team that built and runs the SAGE gallium solar-neutrino experiment, led by Vladimir Gavrin, with Thomas Bowles leading the American side.
summary.technical: Collaboration operating SAGE at Baksan; participants include the Institute for Nuclear Research of the Russian Academy of Sciences (Russia) and Los Alamos National Laboratory (USA); led by Vladimir Gavrin (as of 2017), with Thomas J. Bowles leading the American side; membership counts not found in the sources consulted.
